findings.body: After a hook refuses the initial record commit, the retained fix is invisible to this lookup: its record exists only in the working tree/index, so `story.show` returns no record. `task._new_checkout` creates the worktree and writes that record before committing it (`src/forge/task.py:116–122`; `src/forge/repo.py:494`), while `story.show` reads committed content (`src/forge/story.py:613–616`). Running doctor again therefore skips this fix and creates `forge-files-2`, violating the coordinator's rule against replacement doctor fixes. This is new evidence beyond the retention ruling: retaining the failed checkout works, but recognizing it afterward does not. Extend the record-refusal command test with a second run and recognize the retained checkout without requiring its record to be committed.
findings.title: Not done: doctor keeps at most one fix of its own

findings.body: This preflight compares the current working files using the working copy's configuration, even though the new fix inherits committed `origin/<default>`. In an otherwise synced checkout at that commit, edit only forge.toml's test command without committing it. The workflow now differs from `wanted`, so doctor creates a fix; inside that fix, the original configuration and workflow already match, leaving only the record commit and a permanently retained empty fix. `sync.files` explicitly generates output for the supplied checkout and configuration (`src/forge/sync.py:302–316`). This is new evidence beyond the clean-checkout shortcut ruling: equal commit hashes do not establish that the working configuration matches the default branch. Perform preflight against the committed default-branch files while retaining hand-edit checks against the invoking checkout, and cover this case through the command.
findings.title: Not done: no empty doctor fix is created
